h: Ratho tips: from fun walls to the real thing
p: One of the best things about doing Clip 'n Climb at Ratho is what it can lead to. Plenty of kids who try the fun walls come away buzzing and wanting more, and there's no better place to take that next step, because the arena runs climbing taster sessions and courses for beginners on its proper walls. If you've got a budding climber in the family, have a look at what's on offer while you're there.

For the Clip 'n Climb session itself, a bit of prep helps. Each climber needs a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and it's easiest to do online before you set off. Check the age guidance when booking, as there's usually a minimum age and supervision rules for little ones.

Allow a couple of hours, as the building is big and you'll want time to find your way, get harnessed and sit through the briefing without rushing. Eat light, bring water and wear trainers with comfy clothes.

Ratho is on the western edge of the city, close to the airport and the Gyle, so it's easy to reach by car. Edinburgh Zoo, out at Corstorphine, is one of the nearest big days out for families, and the Union Canal towpath can be followed east from Ratho towards the city if anyone fancies a longer walk or cycle. Further west, Linlithgow Palace, the ruined birthplace of Mary Queen of Scots, makes a cracking historic detour.
